primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Anterior/superior malalignment of the infundibular (outlet) septum produces a large malaligned ventricular septal defect, overriding aorta, and subpulmonary right-ventricular outflow obstruction; right-ventricular hypertrophy develops secondarily.
vignette: An infant has episodic cyanosis that worsens with crying. Echocardiography shows a large malaligned ventricular septal defect, an overriding aorta, right-ventricular outflow obstruction, and right-ventricular hypertrophy.
lead: Which anatomic abnormality most directly underlies this constellation of lesions?
correct: Anterior and superior displacement of the infundibular septum
distractors: Failure of endocardial cushions to fuse in the atrioventricular canal
Complete failure of the embryonic truncus arteriosus to septate
Premature closure of the foramen ovale during fetal life
Failure of the left ventricle to form from the primitive ventricle
distractor_notes: Endocardial-cushion fusion defects cause atrioventricular septal defects, not the characteristic TOF malalignment and RV outflow obstruction.
Complete failure of truncal septation causes persistent truncus arteriosus with a single arterial trunk rather than TOF.
Premature foramen-ovale closure can alter fetal hemodynamics but does not generate the four defining TOF lesions.
The left ventricle derives largely from the primitive ventricle; failure of its formation would cause a different severe developmental anomaly, not TOF.
key_expl: Tetralogy of Fallot is centered on anterior malalignment/deviation of the infundibular septum. This creates subpulmonary right-ventricular outflow obstruction and a malaligned VSD with an overriding aorta. The severity of cyanosis depends largely on the degree of right-ventricular outflow obstruction; right-ventricular hypertrophy is secondary.
objective: Relate the anatomy of tetralogy of Fallot to anterior/superior displacement of the infundibular septum.
